chapters.title: Chapter 1: Why These Three Documents Matter

lessons.title: The Paper Trail: How Your Income and Tax Reach the Income Tax Department

children.text: Priya is a software engineer in Pune earning ₹18 lakh a year. She has a fixed deposit with SBI, holds HDFC Bank shares in her Zerodha account, and sold some mutual fund units in January. She has never written to the Income Tax Department about any of this. Yet when she logs in to the e-filing portal in June, the department already knows her salary, her FD interest, her dividends and her mutual fund sale, down to the rupee.

This is not surveillance magic. It is a reporting system that runs all year, and once you see how it works, Form 16, Form 26AS and AIS stop looking like three confusing PDFs. They become three views of the same trail.
Your PAN Is the Thread
Every rupee that gets reported to the department is tagged to a
PAN

. Your employer quotes it when it deducts tax from your salary. Your bank quotes it when it reports your interest. Your broker and your mutual fund registrar quote it when you sell. The department simply collects everything filed against your PAN and stitches it together.

markDefs.definition: Permanent Account Number: the 10-character alphanumeric ID issued by the Income Tax Department that links all your taxable transactions.

body.text: If your employer or bank has the wrong PAN on record, the tax they deduct lands against someone else's PAN or does not appear at all. You will not see the credit, and you cannot claim it in your return until the deductor corrects it. Check your PAN on your payslip and bank profile once a year.

children.text: Who Reports Your Income: The Four Sources
1. Deductors: Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)
A
deductor

cuts tax before paying you and deposits it with the government. Your employer does this on salary under section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 192 of the 1961 Act). Your bank does it on FD interest and a listed company does it on dividends under section 393 (sections 194A and 194 of the 1961 Act).

markDefs.definition: Any person or entity that is legally required to deduct TDS before making a payment, such as an employer, bank or company. Every deductor has a TAN.

children.text: Depositing the money is only half the job. Every quarter, the deductor files a TDS statement that lists each payee's PAN, the amount paid and the tax deducted. For salary this was Form 24Q, and for most other payments Form 26Q. This quarterly statement is what actually puts the credit against your PAN.
2. Collectors: Tax Collected at Source (TCS)

Some sellers and banks collect tax from you instead of deducting it from a payment to you. Send more than ₹10 lakh abroad in a year under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, or book certain overseas tour packages, and the bank or tour operator collects TCS under section 394 (section 206C of the 1961 Act). That TCS is also filed quarterly against your PAN, and you get credit for it when you file.
3. Reporting Entities: Statement of Financial Transactions (SFT)
This is the source most people have never heard of. Banks, mutual fund registrars such as CAMS and KFintech, depositories, companies and property registrars must file a
Statement of Financial Transactions
under section 508 (section 285BA of the 1961 Act). No tax is deducted here. They simply report what happened.

markDefs.definition: An annual statement (SFT) in which banks, fund houses, registrars and others report specified high-value transactions and income details against your PAN. Filed by 31 May for the previous year.

children.text: SFT covers two kinds of information. The first is high-value transactions, such as cash deposits of ₹10 lakh or more in a year across savings accounts, or a property purchase of ₹30 lakh or more. The second is routine income data such as interest, dividends and sales of shares and mutual fund units, which is reported even when no TDS was deducted.
4. You: Taxes You Pay Yourself
When you pay advance tax or self-assessment tax through the e-filing portal, the challan is recorded against your PAN too. This is the only part of the trail you create directly.

children.text: Why AIS Knows More Than Form 26AS

Here is the part that catches people out. Say Priya's SBI FD earned ₹38,000 of interest in the year. Banks deduct TDS on FD interest only when it crosses ₹50,000 a year for a non-senior citizen, so no TDS was deducted and nothing shows as a tax credit. But SBI still reports that interest through SFT. So the interest appears in her AIS even though her Form 26AS shows nothing for SBI.

Triggered only when tax is actually deducted or collected
Creates a tax credit you can claim

columns.label: Statement of Financial Transactions
points: Filed once a year, by 31 May
Reports income and high-value transactions even with zero TDS
Creates no tax credit, only information

body.text: By the time you sit down to file, the department already has most of your income on record. Your return is not the first word on your income. It is checked against the trail.

children.text: One Year of the Trail

body.title: How Priya's FY 2025-26 salary TDS travelled

events.title: Salary paid, TDS deducted
events.description: Her employer deducts TDS from April salary based on her estimated annual tax.

events.title: TDS deposited
events.description: The employer deposits April's TDS with the government by the 7th of the following month. March TDS gets extra time, until 30 April.

events.title: Q1 TDS statement filed
events.description: The employer files Form 24Q for April to June. Priya's credit for those months now sits against her PAN.

events.title: Q2 and Q3 statements filed
events.description: The same process repeats for July to September and October to December.

events.title: Q4 TDS statement and SFT filed
events.description: The employer files the last quarter. Banks, registrars and depositories file their annual SFT for the year.

events.title: Form 16 issued
events.description: The employer downloads Part A from the TRACES portal and gives Priya her Form 16 by this date.

events.title: Priya reconciles and files
events.description: She checks Form 16 against Form 26AS and AIS, then files her return by the due date, normally 31 July for salaried individuals.

stats.label: Form 16 deadline
stats.context: After the end of the financial year

body.text: Notice the gap. Q4 TDS statements are due on 31 May and Form 16 on 15 June. If you download Form 26AS or AIS in early May, the March quarter is usually missing. For a complete picture, wait until mid-June before you start reconciling.

children.text: From Raw Filings to Your Three Documents
The department does not hand you thousands of raw filings. It compiles them into three documents, each built for a different job:
Form 16
is issued by your employer. It shows the salary TDS your employer filed against your PAN, plus how your salary and tax were worked out.
Form 26AS
is generated by the department. It is your tax credit statement: every rupee of TDS and TCS against your PAN, from every deductor and collector, along with refunds paid to you.
AIS (Annual Information Statement)
is also generated by the department. It is the widest view, adding SFT information such as interest, dividends and securities sales, plus your advance tax and self-assessment tax payments.
The next lesson takes each of these apart. For now, remember the direction of flow: payers report, the department compiles, and you verify.

body.title: New Act, new names: what changes from Tax Year 2026-27

children.text: The Income-tax Act, 2025 took effect on 1 April 2026, along with the Income-tax Rules, 2026. The trail works the same way, but several section and form numbers change for income earned from Tax Year 2026-27 onward. Returns for FY 2025-26, filed in 2026, still use the old names.
Lesson 3 of this chapter covers these changes in detail. Through this course we use the familiar names first and give the new ones alongside.
Check Your Understanding

body.title: Where does untaxed interest show up?
body.question: Priya earned ₹38,000 of FD interest from SBI and no TDS was deducted. Where is this interest most likely to appear?
options: Form 16, because it covers all her income
Form 26AS, as a TDS credit from SBI
AIS, through the bank's Statement of Financial Transactions
Nowhere, because no tax was deducted
body.explanation: Form 16 covers only salary from the employer. Form 26AS shows tax credits, and there was no tax deducted. SBI still reports the interest through SFT, so it appears in AIS.

body.title: The common thread
body.textWithBlank: Employers, banks, brokers and registrars all tag what they report to your ___, which is how the department links everything to you.
body.explanation: Every TDS statement, TCS statement and SFT entry is filed against your PAN. A wrong PAN breaks the link.

body.title: Expected credit from your employer
body.prompt: Priya's employer deducted ₹14,500 of TDS from her salary every month from April 2025 to March 2026. Assuming all four quarterly statements were filed correctly, what total salary TDS credit should Form 26AS show against her employer's TAN?
body.explanation: ₹14,500 × 12 months = ₹1,74,000. If Form 26AS shows less, one or more quarterly statements is missing or wrong, and the employer needs to fix it.

body.title: Rahul's missing interest
body.scenario: Rahul, a first-time filer in Bengaluru, files his return using only his Form 16. He ignores his savings account interest of ₹14,000 and a mutual fund redemption through his Zerodha Coin account, because no TDS was deducted on either. A few months later he receives an intimation that his income has been adjusted.
body.prompt: Why did the department notice, and what should Rahul have done before filing?
body.modelAnswer: His bank reported the savings interest and the fund registrar reported the redemption through SFT, so both appeared in his AIS even without TDS. The processing system compared his return with that information and found income missing. Before filing, Rahul should have downloaded Form 26AS and AIS, matched every entry with his own records, and reported the interest and any capital gain from the redemption. Missing TDS never means missing information.

cards.definition: Tax Deducted at Source. Tax cut by the payer, such as an employer or bank, before paying you, and deposited against your PAN.
Tax Collected at Source. Tax collected from you by a seller or bank on certain transactions, such as large foreign remittances.
Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number. The 10-character number every deductor or collector must quote in its TDS and TCS filings.
Statement of Financial Transactions. An annual report from banks, registrars and others of high-value transactions and income details, even where no TDS applies.
The return a deductor files every quarter listing payees, amounts and TDS. It is what puts the credit against your PAN.
The TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System. The portal where deductors file corrections and download Form 16 Part A.

body.label: Income Tax e-Filing Portal
body.description: Log in with your PAN to view Form 26AS and the Annual Information Statement for any year.

points: Your PAN links every report made about your income, so a wrong PAN with any deductor breaks the trail.
Four sources feed the trail: deductors (TDS), collectors (TCS), reporting entities (SFT) and your own tax payments.
TDS credits reach your PAN only when the deductor files its quarterly statement, not when it deducts.
SFT reports interest, dividends and securities sales even when no tax is deducted, so AIS shows more than Form 26AS.
Wait until mid-June before reconciling, since Q4 TDS statements are due 31 May and Form 16 by 15 June.
From Tax Year 2026-27, the forms carry new numbers under the Income-tax Act, 2025, but the trail works the same way.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and reflects the rules as of September 2026. Thresholds and form numbers can change through Budgets and CBDT notifications. For your specific situation, check the e-filing portal or consult a chartered accountant.
